| **Judg 14:19, 1Sa 11:6, 11:13** (the "Batch A §2.4 refinement") | The two "Spirit rushed upon" verses differ in what the anger comes from. **Saul:** the anger is kindled "when he heard these words", the threat to Jabesh (1Sa 11:6). It ends in mercy that gives the day to God: "Not a man shall be put to death this day, for today the Lord has worked salvation in Israel" (11:13). **Samson:** the Spirit's rushing goes with the striking at Ashkelon. The "hot anger" comes at the end, and the passage gives its ground. His wife wept "You only hate me; you do not love me" (14:16). He told her "because she pressed him hard" (14:17). His own word is "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle" (14:18). Then "Samson's wife was given to his companion" (14:20) | Ch 6 and 10.13 tell both. **10.13 lists Judg 14:19 under "The Spirit of God comes with anger".** The passage puts Samson's anger with being betrayed through his wife, not with the Spirit. That is a fitting to be corrected (rule 77). The deception, a wife's tears as pressure, and the anger at being outwitted are inner-being content not yet told |

| **Act 7:54** (the M47 tag on "enraged") | "they were enraged" is *diapriō* ("to be sawn through", G1282) with *kardia* ("heart"). "they ground their teeth at him" puts the anger in the body. Against them stands Stephen, "full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven" (7:55) | The heart is told in Ch 4 (*"sawn through in their hearts"*). The tag question is closed: the M47 token is the heart word itself. **The teeth are not told** (see §2) |
| **Rom 13:5** (conscience as a seat) | Two grounds for subjection side by side: "to avoid God's wrath" and "for the sake of conscience" | Told in Ch 8, 10.13 and 10.14 |

| **Eze 21:15** (the context seat) | "that their hearts may melt, and many stumble. At all their gates I have given the glittering sword". The melting heart is what the sword is given *for*. It is fear aimed at the heart by God | Uncited. It goes beside Eze 21:7 (now in 10.12 *Fear in the body*), in 10.12 *Dread laid on others* |

| **The unit 2 revisit notes** to §12, §13, §25, §34 | Their verses: Jer 44 (§12), Jon 3:9 (§13), Col 3:6 (§25), Hab 2:15–16 and the cup (§34) | All told (10.2, 10.13, Ch 12, Ch 14, 10.0).
